benchmark_hit_summary.basis: F-0012 points directly at hmac_core.sv:223-230. Phase3 confirms SHA2_512 falls into the default branch and uses BlockSizeSHA512in64 + 64'd384 instead of + 64'd512.

F-0016 is misworded about cfg_block being set on start, but it lands on the correct cfg_block path. Phase3 confirms the real bug is hmac.sv:365-372 clearing cfg_block on reg_hash_stop before completion.

The findings touch the idle/done_state completion path but do not explicitly identify the 127-cycle cool_down delay. Phase3 tracing of hmac.sv:180-188 and hmac.sv:891-903 confirms the stale-completion bug.

F-0010 is wrong about non-zero wipe data being the problem, but it points to the wipe_secret path. Phase3 confirms the real issue is hmac_reg_top.sv:2128 gating wipe_secret_we with reg_error instead of !reg_error.

These findings all land on the err_valid/err_code priority path, but none states the exact root cause. Phase3 confirms hmac.sv:842-845 includes invalid_config_atstart in err_valid while hmac.sv:850-875 omits it from the priority case.

F-0017 is framed as a width issue, but it points to msg_allowed. Phase3 confirms hmac.sv:414-420 never clears msg_allowed on hash_stop, so post-stop MSG_FIFO writes and message_length updates remain possible through hmac.sv:628 and hmac.sv:658-660.

F-0016 reaches the cfg_block lock path but states the wrong polarity problem. Phase3 confirms the real defect is the premature unlock on reg_hash_stop at hmac.sv:365-372, which reopens config/key/context writes before the engine is idle.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: The WIPE_SECRET write strobe is generated as `(addr_hit[8] && reg_we && reg_error)` in hmac_reg_top.sv:2128. The top module only treats `reg2hw.wipe_secret.qe` as the wipe trigger (hmac.sv:210), and only overwrites `secret_key_d` when that trigger is high (hmac.sv:214-217). Ordinary software writes therefore do not start a wipe at all.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: A normal software write to WIPE_SECRET at offset 0x20 with no bus error.
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: Secret key and related internal state can survive an intended wipe, breaking zeroization and enabling reuse of stale keyed state in later operations.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: In the final-hash branch, the `unique case` handles SHA2_256 and SHA2_384 explicitly, but routes SHA2_512 through the default branch, which sets `sha_msg_len = BlockSizeSHA512in64 + 64'd384` instead of `+ 64'd512`.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: HMAC mode, second round (`sel_msglen == SelOPadMsg` / outer round), digest_size_i == SHA2_512.
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: The SHA-512 HMAC final block is padded with the wrong message length, producing incorrect authentication results.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: err_valid includes `invalid_config_atstart` in hmac.sv:842-845, but the priority case that drives err_code never handles that condition. Instead it repeats `hash_start_sha_disabled` twice at hmac.sv:851-858. When invalid_config_atstart is the only active cause, the interrupt asserts but err_code falls through to NoError.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: Software issues hash_start or hash_continue with invalid digest/key configuration, while no higher-priority error cause is active.
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: The module signals an error event without reporting the real cause, weakening software diagnostics and fault-detection coverage for invalid configuration attempts.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: cfg_block is cleared whenever `reg_hash_done || reg_hash_stop` is true (hmac.sv:370-371). `reg_hash_stop` is only the command pulse decoded at hmac.sv:349, not a completion signal. Clearing cfg_block immediately re-enables key and configuration writes in update_secret_key (hmac.sv:218-225) and CSR message-length writes (hmac.sv:647-653) before hashing is actually finished.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: Software writes CMD.hash_stop while a hash operation is still active.
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: The module opens a premature write window for key/config/context state during an in-flight stop, allowing corruption of the running operation and unsafe context-switch timing.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: msg_allowed is set on hash_start_or_continue and only cleared on packer_flush_done (hmac.sv:417-420). A hash_stop command does not clear it. As a result, msg_write remains legal through hmac.sv:628 and message_length keeps incrementing through hmac.sv:658-660 after stop. The `msg_push_not_allowed` error path at hmac.sv:813 also stays inactive because msg_allowed never drops.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: Software issues CMD.hash_stop and then continues writing MSG_FIFO before a new start/continue cycle.
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: The stopped message stream is not frozen: software can still inject message words and mutate the saved message length after stop, breaking context-switch and finalization semantics.

confirmed_bugs.root_cause: After hash_stop, the done_state machine waits for `!hash_running` and then intentionally delays `hash_done_event` for 127 cycles (hmac.sv:180-188). Top-level idle/status, however, is driven only by FIFO emptiness and sub-core idle signals (hmac.sv:891-903) and is not held off by done_state or the cool_down counter.
confirmed_bugs.trigger_condition: Stop-driven context-switch flow: software stops hashing, observes STATUS.hmac_idle / idle_o, and acts before the delayed hmac_done event arrives.
confirmed_bugs.security_impact: Software can observe idle and restore or read context before the official completion event, creating a stale-completion window that can expose or mix old digest/context state across message streams.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] Spec assumption indicates alerts[0] is an input port driven by external logic, but the implementation guarantee shows it is an output port driven by an internal bus integ
per_finding_results.summary: There is no alert-bus wiring bug here. The design only has one alert, so alerts[0] is the only legal request bit and is intentionally driven from hmac_reg_top.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_reg_pkg.sv:12 fixes NumAlerts=1. hmac.sv:778 drives alerts[0] from u_reg.intg_err_o, and hmac.sv:788-801 instantiates exactly one alert sender consuming that bit.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding assumes a multi-bit alert request bus with unused bits. That assumption is false in this IP because NumAlerts is 1. The top-level alert_rx_i is the external interface; alerts[0] is an internal request wire into prim_alert_sender.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] The actual functional guarantees of signals like hash_running, digest_on_blk, sha_hash_done, and sha_core_idle depend en
per_finding_results.summary: This is a scope note, not a defect. The finding says some signals depend on prim_sha2_32 internals, but that does not identify a bug in the HMAC RTL.
per_finding_results.root_cause: The HMAC RTL simply consumes these signals through explicit ports at hmac.sv:735-760 and uses them in the local state machines.
per_finding_results.reasoning: A dependency on a submodule implementation is normal. After reviewing prim_sha2_32.sv, the connected signals are driven synchronously and are used consistently by hmac.sv and hmac_core.sv.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] Assumption states signals i_pad_256/512 and o_pad_256/512 are inputs driven externally, but the implementation drives them as internal outputs. This will result in a mult
per_finding_results.summary: The pads are supposed to be internal combinational values, not externally driven inputs. The zeroed Key_1024 SHA-256 pad case is also blocked by invalid_config logic.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:129-187 intentionally derives i_pad_256/i_pad_512/o_pad_256/o_pad_512 from secret_key_i and key_length_i. hmac.sv:818-820 blocks Key_1024 with SHA2_256 in HMAC mode.
per_finding_results.reasoning: There is no multi-driver condition. The finding's external-driver assumption is wrong, and the potentially dangerous Key_1024 plus SHA2_256 combination is already rejected before hashing starts.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] Are the inputs fifo_empty, fifo_full, and fifo_full_seen_d synchronous to clk_i? If they originate from a different cloc
per_finding_results.summary: The FIFO status path is synchronous to clk_i in this IP. There is no clock-domain crossing on fifo_empty or fifo_full here.
per_finding_results.root_cause: interfaces.md:5-7 declares only one clock. hmac.sv:545 derives fifo_empty from fifo_rvalid, and hmac.sv:568-590 instantiates prim_fifo_sync on clk_i/rst_ni to generate fifo_full/fifo_rvalid.
per_finding_results.reasoning: Both the FIFO and the tracking flops at hmac.sv:485-494 run on clk_i. The metastability concern depends on a second clock that does not exist in this IP boundary.

per_finding_results.title: Priority order places update_seckey_inprocess (secret-key related) at the lowest priority; if it co-occurs with higher-p
per_finding_results.summary: The finding's specific complaint about update_seckey_inprocess priority is not the real bug. However, the same err_valid/err_code priority path is genuinely broken because invalid_config_atstart can raise an error interrupt while ERR_CODE remains NoError.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:842-845 includes invalid_config_atstart in err_valid. hmac.sv:850-875 never encodes invalid_config_atstart and instead duplicates hash_start_sha_disabled at hmac.sv:851-858, so the case falls through to NoError.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: hash_start or hash_continue is written with invalid digest/key configuration and no higher-priority error cause is active.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Software and fault-detection logic can observe an error interrupt without the true error code, weakening detection of invalid configuration attempts.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The stated update_seckey priority concern is not independently a bug because the design intentionally reports one cause. But tracing the exact same priority tree shows a real omission: invalid_config_atstart asserts err_valid yet is missing from the err_code case tree.
additional_findings: Same underlying bug as F-0014 and F-0022.

per_finding_results.title: The loop maps reg2hw.key[31-i] to secret_key_d word i, reversing the natural order. The design intent (endianness handli
per_finding_results.summary: The apparent reversal is intentional and matches the documented KEY register ordering.
per_finding_results.root_cause: registers.md:351-353 defines key[1023:0] = {KEY0, KEY1, ..., KEY31}. hmac.sv:220-224 maps reg2hw.key[31-i] into secret_key_d[32*i+:32], which reconstructs that packed ordering for hmac_core.sv consumers.
per_finding_results.reasoning: hmac_core.sv uses secret_key_i[1023:896] as the high-order words for short keys, so KEY0 must end up in the high bits. The load loop does exactly that.

per_finding_results.title: The RTL uses txcount[BlockSizeBitsSHA512-1:...] and similar bit slices that require txcount to be at least BlockSizeBitsSHA512 bits wide. No guarantee exists to verify that txcount is actually declare
per_finding_results.summary: txcount is declared as a 64-bit counter, so all referenced slices are legal.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:69 declares `logic [63:0] txcount, txcount_d;`. The largest slice used is hmac_core.sv:126 and hmac_core.sv:241-242, which is far smaller than 64 bits.
per_finding_results.reasoning: This finding is purely disproved by the declaration width. There is no out-of-bounds risk from txcount's declared size.

per_finding_results.title: pad_index_256 直接从 txcount 的高位切片得到，无任何饱和限幅或范围检查。当 txcount 对应的块内字偏移超过 15 时，该索引将越界访问 i_pad_256/o_pad_256 数组，读取未定义数据，可能泄露密钥材料或产生错误的 HMAC 结果。
per_finding_results.summary: The control FSM does not consume pad data beyond the legal block range. The index concern does not become an observable functional bug on this path.
per_finding_results.root_cause: pad_index_256 comes from hmac_core.sv:127 and is only relevant when sel_rdata selects pad data at hmac_core.sv:194-201. The FSM stops asserting hmac_sha_rvalid once txcnt_eq_blksz is true at hmac_core.sv:354-362 and hmac_core.sv:433-441.
per_finding_results.reasoning: During the final legal pad word transfer, txcount is 480 for SHA-256 and pad_index_256 is 15. On the next cycle txcount reaches 512, but valid is deasserted and the state advances, so the putative out-of-range data is not consumed by the SHA path.

per_finding_results.title: The design lacks any mechanism to ensure that msg_write and sha_en are de-asserted when packer_ready is low. If external logic violates the intended coherence, data can be written while the HMAC engin
per_finding_results.summary: The valid/ready handshake already prevents acceptance and counting when the packer is not ready.
per_finding_results.root_cause: u_packer consumes data only on valid_i/ready_o handshake at hmac.sv:674-696, and message_length increments only when msg_write, sha_en, and packer_ready are all true at hmac.sv:656-660. tlul_adapter_sram grant is also gated by packer_ready at hmac.sv:531.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding assumes data is accepted without ready. That is not how the interface is wired: when packer_ready is low, the write is neither packed nor counted.

per_finding_results.title: 擦除值wipe_v由软件可编程寄存器直接驱动，未硬连线为0。若软件配置为非零值，在擦除操作期间secret_key_d将被写入非零常量，无法保证敏感密钥数据被可靠清零，存在残留风险。
per_finding_results.summary: The finding's stated reason is wrong: WIPE_SECRET is intentionally allowed to use any 32-bit overwrite pattern. But the same wipe_secret signal path contains a real bug: ordinary software writes do not trigger the wipe at all.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_reg_top.sv:2128 defines `wipe_secret_we = (addr_hit[8] && reg_we && reg_error)`. hmac.sv:210 uses `reg2hw.wipe_secret.qe` as the wipe trigger, and hmac.sv:214-217 only overwrites secret_key_d when that trigger is high. Normal writes with reg_error=0 therefore skip the wipe.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: A legal software write to WIPE_SECRET with no TL/register error.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Secret state can persist across an intended wipe, violating zeroization and enabling reuse of stale keyed state.
per_finding_results.reasoning: registers.md:326-332 explicitly documents overwrite-with-provided-value behavior, so non-zero wipe_v is not itself a defect. The real defect is the inverted write-enable gate in hmac_reg_top, which prevents the documented wipe operation from running on normal accesses.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] digest_size_supplied is formed by casting cfg_reg.digest_size.q to digest_mode_e without verifying the raw value is a le
per_finding_results.summary: Illegal digest encodings are handled defensively, not unsafely.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:296-309 casts the field, then maps unsupported values to SHA2_None. hmac.sv:818-823 treats SHA2_None as invalid_config and blocks start/continue.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding points to the cast, but the following case statement explicitly sanitizes the value before it can drive hashing behavior.

per_finding_results.title: In the final hash branch, for SHA2_384 and the default/SHA2_512 cases, sha_msg_len is BlockSizeSHA512in64 + 64'd384. For
per_finding_results.summary: This is a real functional bug. SHA-512 outer-round message length is computed with the SHA-384 digest-size constant.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:223-230 handles SHA2_256 and SHA2_384 explicitly, but leaves SHA2_512 to the default branch, which sets `sha_msg_len = BlockSizeSHA512in64 + 64'd384`.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: HMAC mode outer round with digest_size_i == SHA2_512.
per_finding_results.security_impact: The final SHA-512 HMAC digest is wrong because the padded message length field is wrong by 128 bits.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The units are bits, not bytes, so the bug is not in unit conversion. The actual defect is simpler: SHA2_512 is never given a 512-bit digest contribution in the outer-round message-length calculation.

per_finding_results.title: When hmac_en_i is 1, sha_hash_process_o is formed by OR-ing reg_hash_process_i and hash_process. The purpose of this OR
per_finding_results.summary: The OR is intentional and needed to support both the software-requested process event and the internal outer-round transition.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:123 drives sha_hash_process_o from `reg_hash_process_i | hash_process` in HMAC mode. reg_hash_process_i is used for the software finalization path, while hash_process is asserted internally at hmac_core.sv:374 for the outer round.
per_finding_results.reasoning: Without the OR, either the inner-round software finalize path or the outer-round automatic finalize path would be lost. The construction matches the two-phase HMAC flow.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] The branch condition that triggers this err_code assignment is not visible in this chunk; it may be wrongly prioritized
per_finding_results.summary: The err_code priority logic is in fact wrong. invalid_config_atstart can raise err_valid without any matching err_code branch.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:842-845 includes invalid_config_atstart in err_valid, but hmac.sv:850-875 never encodes it. The priority case duplicates hash_start_sha_disabled at hmac.sv:851-858 instead of adding an invalid_config_atstart branch.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: hash_start/hash_continue with invalid digest or key configuration and no other simultaneous error cause.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Software sees an error interrupt but can read ERR_CODE=NoError, obscuring the real fault condition.
per_finding_results.reasoning: This finding correctly suspected the priority path. Full-file review shows the exact defect: the validity condition and the encoded cause table disagree.

per_finding_results.title: conv_endian32 is not defined in this chunk; its exact byte-reordering logic (e.g., for mask bits) must be verified elsew
per_finding_results.summary: Missing local definition in a chunk is not a defect in the RTL. The finding identifies a review dependency, not a bug.
per_finding_results.root_cause: conv_endian32 is a shared helper used consistently at hmac.sv:223, hmac.sv:253-281, hmac.sv:542, hmac.sv:671-672.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The question is about where the helper is defined, not about incorrect use on this path. No contradictory or unsafe behavior was found in the HMAC wiring itself.

per_finding_results.title: 硬件在hash_start或hash_continue命令时错误地将cfg_block驱为1，而设计预期该路径使用cfg_block的反相（即0），导致hash_start/hash_continue功能失效。
per_finding_results.summary: The finding's polarity claim is wrong: setting cfg_block after start/continue is intentional. But the same cfg_block path contains a real bug because hash_stop clears cfg_block before the engine is actually done.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:365-372 clears cfg_block when reg_hash_stop is asserted. reg_hash_stop is only the decoded command pulse from hmac.sv:349, so the lock is dropped immediately, reopening key/config/context writes through hmac.sv:214-226 and hmac.sv:645-653 before completion.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: A stop command is issued while hashing is still in progress.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Software can modify protected state during an in-flight stop, corrupting results and violating context-switch safety.
per_finding_results.reasoning: hash_start and hash_continue are gated by ~cfg_block at hmac.sv:360-361 using the pre-update value, so they still work. The real failure is on the stop side, where cfg_block drops too early.

per_finding_results.title: [U-UP] The assignments use 1'b1 and 1'b0, but the reset uses '0. If msg_allowed is wider than 1 bit, the set/clear assignments only affect the LSB, while the
per_finding_results.summary: The width-mismatch claim is false because msg_allowed is a 1-bit logic. But the same msg_allowed path contains a real stop-handling bug: hash_stop does not clear msg_allowed, so software writes remain allowed after stop.
per_finding_results.root_cause: msg_allowed is declared as a scalar at hmac.sv:125. The real defect is hmac.sv:414-420, which only clears msg_allowed on packer_flush_done and never on reg_hash_stop. msg_write remains enabled at hmac.sv:628 and message_length keeps updating at hmac.sv:658-660.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: CMD.hash_stop followed by further MSG_FIFO writes before a new start/continue sequence.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Post-stop message injection and message-length mutation remain possible, so the stopped context is not frozen.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding lands on the correct register but states the wrong reason. Once the actual sequential logic is traced, the bug is that msg_allowed does not track stop at all.

per_finding_results.title: [U-UP] The integrity error output (intg_error_o) of u_tlul_adapter is left unconnected. TL-UL integrity errors are not monitored or handled.
per_finding_results.summary: The claimed missing top-level TL-UL integrity handling is not real on this path.
per_finding_results.root_cause: Top-level TL-UL command integrity is already checked in hmac_reg_top.sv:51-82 before accesses are steered to the register file or the MSG_FIFO window. The window adapter instance in hmac.sv:593-623 also leaves CmdIntgCheck at its default 0, so it is not the primary external TL integrity checker.
per_finding_results.reasoning: Unconnected intg_error_o on the internal window adapter does not mean the external TL bus is unchecked; that check already happens in hmac_reg_top. The finding overstates the consequence.

per_finding_results.title: [U-UP] The enum base type is `logic`, allowing 4-state values (X, Z); no local mechanism prevents X assignment. If a driver produces X, the selection may sil
per_finding_results.summary: This is a generic 4-state simulation concern, not a concrete RTL bug on this design path.
per_finding_results.root_cause: The relevant enums in hmac_core.sv are locally driven by deterministic combinational logic with explicit defaults, and sel_rdata is further covered by the assertion at hmac_core.sv:498.
per_finding_results.reasoning: A hypothetical X from an arbitrary driver is not evidence of a design defect. No reachable functional bug was found from the actual RTL assignments.

per_finding_results.title: Hardware does not guarantee that digest memory is properly initialized before use. When reg2hw.digest[2*i].qe is low and no prior valid write has occurred, the digest engine may operate on garbage or
per_finding_results.summary: The SHA engine does not consume restore digest data unless digest_sw_we is asserted, so missing SW writes do not automatically feed garbage into the core.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:257-263 only raises digest_sw_we when one of the corresponding digest CSR write-enables is asserted. prim_sha2_32 consumes digest_i together with digest_we_i through hmac.sv:753-755.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding conflates 'no restore write happened' with 'garbage is loaded'. On this interface, the load is explicit and write-enable qualified.

per_finding_results.title: The error output (err_o) of u_msg_fifo is left unconnected. Any FIFO error (e.g., overflow) cannot be detected or handle
per_finding_results.summary: No reachable FIFO-overflow defect was found in the HMAC wiring. The unconnected err_o is not evidence of a functional bug here.
per_finding_results.root_cause: u_msg_fifo is instantiated at hmac.sv:568-590, while all producers are back-pressured by fifo_wready through hmac.sv:546 and hmac.sv:690. The design does not rely on err_o for normal correctness on this path.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding assumes an overflow path without showing one. In the reviewed RTL, all data sources honor fifo_wready before a write is committed.

per_finding_results.title: HMAC模块缺失对err_valid信号的寄存器打拍或相应稳定逻辑，组合逻辑err_code直接驱动err_valid，在输入信号变化时可能产生毛刺，导致中断控制器漏采中断。
per_finding_results.summary: The glitch rationale is not supported, but the same err_valid/err_code path is genuinely broken: invalid_config_atstart can assert err_valid while err_code remains NoError.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:842-845 and hmac.sv:850-875 disagree about invalid_config_atstart. err_valid includes it; err_code never encodes it and instead duplicates hash_start_sha_disabled.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: hash_start/hash_continue with invalid configuration and no other simultaneous error cause.
per_finding_results.security_impact: The error-reporting path can present an interrupt without the actual reason code, reducing diagnostic and security-response fidelity.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The reviewed RTL does not prove a sampling-glitch issue, because the inputs are synchronous control signals. However, tracing the exact same signals reveals a real design bug on that path, so the finding is confirmed under the phase3 same-signal-path rule.
additional_findings: Same underlying bug as F-0005 and F-0014.

per_finding_results.title: idle_d可能因为txcnt_eq_blksz与reg_hash_stop_d组合产生的短脉冲或异步信号而提前拉高，导致idle_o在停止处理尚未真正完成时就指示空闲，使系统错误地认为HMAC已空闲，可能引发后续操作错误。
per_finding_results.summary: The specific short-pulse explanation is wrong, but the completion path really is inconsistent: idle/status can indicate completion before hash_done_event is raised after stop.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:180-188 delays hash_done_event for up to 127 cycles after !hash_running. Meanwhile idle/status is driven independently by hmac.sv:891-903 and does not wait for done_state or the cool_down counter.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: Stop-driven context switching where software observes STATUS.hmac_idle or idle_o before the delayed hmac_done interrupt arrives.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Software can act on an apparently idle engine before the official completion event, creating a stale-completion window for digest/context handling.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The issue is not metastability on idle_d. The real problem is architectural: completion signaling is split into two paths, and the idle path opens earlier than the delayed interrupt path.

per_finding_results.title: sel_rdata 的驱动规范仅描述了 StOPad 和 StIPad 状态的赋值，未覆盖 StIdle、StMsg 等其余状态，无法保证 sel_rdata 在所有条件下均不取 2'b11。若其他状态产生非法编码，将触发假设中描述的 default 路径静默输出 fifo_rdata_i，掩盖控制故障或毛刺。
per_finding_results.summary: sel_rdata is fully covered by defaults and assertions; there is no uncovered 2'b11 path in the reviewed RTL.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:323 sets sel_rdata = SelFifo by default. StIPad and StOPad override it explicitly at hmac_core.sv:352 and hmac_core.sv:430, and hmac_core.sv:498 asserts the legal encoding set.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The default path is not a silent bug mask here; SelFifo is a legal state used in StMsg and idle-like states.

per_finding_results.title: 缺少对复位信号的毛刺抑制或同步器保证，外部干扰可能引起不可靠的复位行为。
per_finding_results.summary: This is an environment-level reset-quality concern, not an RTL bug specific to this IP.
per_finding_results.root_cause: The module consistently uses rst_ni as an asynchronous reset in local flops, for example at hmac.sv:197-208 and hmac_core.sv:308-310.
per_finding_results.reasoning: Nothing in the reviewed HMAC logic indicates a broken reset implementation beyond the generic assumption that rst_ni is a valid reset source.

per_finding_results.title: 组合逻辑中缺少当 load_txcount 有效时 txcount_d 的赋值逻辑，可能导致该信号处于未定义状态，进而使 txcount 寄存器采样到无效值。
per_finding_results.summary: The assignment that the finding claims is missing is present in the RTL.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:258-266 explicitly assigns txcount_d in the load_txcount branch.
per_finding_results.reasoning: This finding is directly disproved by the code in the txcount next-value block.

per_finding_results.title: The state flip-flop specification does not enforce validity of st_d, so an illegal st_d can propagate to st_q, causing the FSM to leave the defined state space and potentially corrupt HMAC operation.
per_finding_results.summary: The FSM has a recovery default back to StIdle, so the claimed lack of any recovery mechanism is wrong.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_core.sv:451-453 assigns st_d = StIdle in the default case, and hmac_core.sv:308-310 registers that state.
per_finding_results.reasoning: An X on st_d is a separate simulation-quality concern, but the finding's claim that the FSM has no illegal-state recovery is contradicted by the default branch.

per_finding_results.title: [B-AG+U-UP] It is not locally verified that message_length_i and the block size constants (BlockSizeSHA256in64, BlockSizeSHA512in64)
per_finding_results.summary: The units match: message_length is tracked in bits, not bytes, so adding 256/384/512-bit digest lengths and 512/1024-bit block sizes is consistent.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:632-636 sums the 32-bit expanded write mask, which counts message bits because each written byte contributes eight mask bits. hmac.sv:658-660 adds that bit count into message_length. hmac_core.sv:217-229 then adds block-size and digest-size constants that are also expressed in bits.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The name BlockSizeSHA256in64 is misleading, but the actual values are 512 and 1024 bits. The surrounding accounting shows the interface is bit-based, so there is no unit mismatch on this path.

per_finding_results.title: A register write one-hot error on u_reg should trigger alert_tx_o[0].
per_finding_results.summary: This behavior is implemented and even asserted locally.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_reg_top.sv:58-82 generates reg_we_err and ORs it into intg_err_o. hmac.sv:778 routes intg_err_o to alerts[0], hmac.sv:796 feeds alerts[0] into the alert sender, and hmac.sv:965 contains ASSERT_PRIM_REG_WE_ONEHOT_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT on alert_tx_o[0].
per_finding_results.reasoning: The assumption in the finding is true and satisfied by the RTL, so there is no bug.

per_finding_results.title: Signal unused_cfg_qe drives an XOR reduction of multiple configuration QE bits, but its usage is not visible in this chu
per_finding_results.summary: unused_cfg_qe is a benign lint-suppression sink, not a functional bug.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac.sv:287-291 reduces otherwise-unused cfg_reg.qe bits into a local wire. No downstream use is required for correctness.
per_finding_results.reasoning: Dead 'unused' reductions are common style in OpenTitan RTL. No control or data path depends on this signal.

per_finding_results.title: [U-UP] The reset initialization uses 'default:'0' to zeroize any fields of the cfg_reg struct not explicitly listed in the assignment. It is unknown whether
per_finding_results.summary: The cfg_reg struct has no hidden extra fields that require non-zero reset values.
per_finding_results.root_cause: hmac_reg_pkg.sv:68-97 shows cfg_reg contains exactly hmac_en, sha_en, endian_swap, digest_swap, key_swap, digest_size, and key_length. hmac.sv:375-407 initializes those explicitly and zeros any padding/default members.
per_finding_results.reasoning: This is resolved by checking the actual struct definition. There are no omitted functional fields.

per_finding_results.title: [U-UP] The byte-alignment assumption is enforced only as a simulation/formal property (disabled by `ifndef VERILATOR / SYNTHESIS`). In synthesized hardware,
per_finding_results.summary: The byte-alignment property is an environment check for the incoming TL-generated mask, not an unguarded hardware hazard in normal operation.
per_finding_results.root_cause: The MSG_FIFO path is sourced from tlul_adapter_sram in hmac.sv:593-623, which generates the mask from TL byte lanes. The property at hmac.sv:911-919 checks that environment invariant during non-synthesis verification.
per_finding_results.reasoning: No local RTL path was found that can synthesize an arbitrary non-byte-aligned mask on its own. The finding overstates the significance of the assertion guard.

per_finding_results.title: [U-UP] The enum `done_state_e` defines four states for done handling, but no transition conditions or FSM behavior are specified in this chunk; design intent
per_finding_results.summary: The chunk-visibility complaint is not itself a bug, but the same done_state signal path contains a real completion defect: hmac_done is intentionally delayed after idle opens.
per_finding_results.root_cause: The done_state FSM in hmac.sv:149-195 delays hash_done_event by a 127-cycle cool-down at hmac.sv:180-188, while idle/status is independently exposed by hmac.sv:891-903.
per_finding_results.trigger_condition: Stop-based completion where software trusts STATUS.hmac_idle / idle_o before the delayed hmac_done event.
per_finding_results.security_impact: Stale completion ordering can let software restore or inspect context too early, creating cross-stream digest/context confusion.
per_finding_results.reasoning: Reading the full file resolves the 'unspecified FSM' concern, and that full-file read also exposes a real flaw on the exact done_state path. Under the phase3 rule, that makes the finding confirmed.
additional_findings: Same underlying bug as F-0023; matches benchmark 011 partially.

per_finding_results.title: Internal signals reg2hw, hw2reg, tl_win_h2d, tl_win_d2h are declared but neither driven nor assigned in this chunk; thei
per_finding_results.summary: These are normal interconnect signals whose drivers appear elsewhere in the same module and instances.
per_finding_results.root_cause: reg2hw/hw2reg are connected through hmac_reg_top at hmac.sv:764-779. tl_win_h2d/tl_win_d2h are connected between hmac_reg_top and tlul_adapter_sram at hmac.sv:599-603 and hmac.sv:771-772.
per_finding_results.reasoning: The finding only reflects chunk incompleteness. The full module contains the missing drivers and connections.
